changes: Updated p2's evidence to cite both scribal statements ('...śrīmaheśvarānandena samarpita' and 'maheśvarānanden likhita'). Kept the role as scribe only.
Notes: added that 'samarpita' could imply he dedicated or presented the copy. Donor was not added because the colophon does not say so explicitly.
Notes: added that Māgha śukla 3 of VS 1949 falls in Jan/Feb 1893 CE, so ce_approx 1893 is kept.
Notes: added that the colophon gives two different granthasaṃkhyā figures (9500 and 1831), and that the text title appears as 'bhīmavinode'.
Notes: added that Lalitāpuranagara is grammatically the scribe's place of residence. The catalogue treats it as the place of copying.

persons.name: Maheśvarānanda
persons.evidence: likhitṃ śrīlalitāpuranagasya (!) mahābauddhopāśaka (!) śrīmaheśvarānandena samarpita; maheśvarānanden likhita

notes: The catalogue gives SAM1959, but the colophon reads saṃvat 1949. The era is taken as Vikrama because of the Nepali 'sāla miti' formula. Māgha śukla 3 of VS 1949 falls in Jan/Feb 1893 CE. In the colophon, Lalitāpuranagara (Patan) is in the genitive and describes the scribe ('of Lalitāpuranagara'), so strictly it is his residence. It is very probably also the place of copying. 'samarpita' might mean the scribe offered or presented the copy, but donor has not been assigned. The colophon gives two different granthasaṃkhyā figures (9500 and 1831). The text is called 'bhīmavinoda' here, while the catalogue title is Bhīmasenavinoda.
